title: Solving simple fractional equations reducible to linear equations
summary: Clear denominators with a common multiple, then solve and check the resulting linear equation.
objectives: Identify a lowest common multiple for all denominators.
Multiply every term by the same common multiple.
Solve the resulting linear equation and verify it in the original fractional equation.

blocks.text: A fractional equation with numerical denominators can be converted into an equivalent linear equation by multiplying every term on both sides by a common multiple of all denominators. The lowest common multiple usually keeps the numbers smallest.
The lowest common multiple is 12. Multiplying every complete term by 12 gives 4(x + 1) - 3(x - 2) = 60. Mark each cancelled denominator so that no term is missed.

sections.title: Treat each numerator as one grouped expression

blocks.text: A fraction bar groups its whole numerator. When the numerator contains more than one term, keep brackets after clearing the denominator. A minus sign before a fraction subtracts the entire numerator, so it must distribute to every term when brackets are expanded.
Writing -(x - 3) as -x - 3 is incorrect because the sign of -3 must also reverse. Delay expansion until all denominators have been cancelled; this makes the structure easier to audit.

sections.title: Solve the linear equation, then check the fractions

blocks.text: After denominators are cleared, expand brackets, collect like terms and solve as in an ordinary linear equation. The clearing step is valid because the common multiple is a non-zero number, so the transformed equation has the same solutions.

Verify the answer in the original fractional equation rather than only in the cleared version. Simplify each fraction separately and confirm that the two original sides match. This check catches a missed term or a bracket-sign error.

sections.title: Worked example: use the lowest common multiple

content.text: The lowest common multiple of 3 and 2 is 6. Multiply every term by 6.

sections.verification_note: Substituting x = 7 into the original equation gives 9/3 + 6/2 = 3 + 3 = 6.

sections.title: Worked example: preserve brackets during subtraction

content.text: The lowest common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12. Multiply every term by 12.
Expand both grouped numerators, including the subtraction.

sections.verification_note: For x = 4, the original left side is 7/4 - 6/6 = 7/4 - 1 = 3/4, matching the right side.

feedback.text: Multiplying both sides by 5 gives x - 4 = 15, so x = 19.

blocks.text: Find a common multiple of every denominator and multiply every complete term on both sides. Keep brackets around multi-term numerators and distribute subtraction signs carefully.
Solve the resulting linear equation, then substitute into the original fractional equation to check that both sides have the same value.
